### P1-03K React Server Components contract review — 2026-10-24

**Directive inventory.** No React-owned source file under `packages/react/src` has a leading `'use client'` or `"use client"` directive. This includes the package root barrel (`src/index.ts`), the ribbon subpath barrel (`src/components/ribbon/index.ts`), and `FindReplaceDialog.tsx`. The emitted browser JavaScript also has no such directive. The packed Node files `dist/node/index.js`, `dist/node/components/ribbon/index.js`, and `dist/node/components/dialogs/FindReplaceDialog.js` contain zero directive occurrences. The Node target therefore does not preserve or relocate a package-owned client boundary; none exists in the source to preserve.

The P1-03I build log `/tmp/cs002d4-p1-03i-build.log` contains 152 Vite 8.3.4 `MODULE_LEVEL_DIRECTIVE` warnings: 76 while producing `dist/node/index.js`, 76 while producing `dist/node/components/ribbon/index.js`, and none while producing `dist/node/components/dialogs/FindReplaceDialog.js`. Their warning sources are third-party `@fluentui/react-icons/lib/icons/chunk-*.js`, `@fluentui/react-icons/lib/sizedIcons/chunk-*.js`, and `@griffel/react/src/*.js` modules. Vite states those module-level directives may not be preserved. These warnings do not refer to React package source. Inspection confirms the resulting package JS files contain no `use client` directive, including the affected bundled Node outputs. They are nonfatal for the qualified Node import/SSR behavior, but mean those bundles cannot supply framework-recognized RSC client references for those dependencies either.

**Client-only API inventory.** The root barrel re-exports the stateful React UI broadly: `CyberSheet`, `ExcelApp`, `BackstageContainer`, ribbon and backstage components, dialogs, overlays, and hooks/configuration providers. `CyberSheet` uses React state, refs, effects, context, and imperative handles; its `CanvasRenderer` construction is in an effect and its interaction code uses DOM event listeners, `ResizeObserver`, and animation-frame APIs. `CustomCellOverlay` uses hooks and `react-dom` portals. The ribbon barrel exports both hooks and interactive components. `FindReplaceDialog` is a stateful dialog component. Other exported modules also use effects, context, event handlers, and browser APIs such as `window` and `document`. Their source modules and package root do not mark these client components for RSC graph partitioning.

The qualified traditional SSR result remains compatible with this source design because ordinary `renderToString()` and streaming render do not execute effects. It does not answer whether a framework can recognize package exports as client references when those exports are imported directly into an RSC server graph. The native Node resolution condition selects the Node bundles for server imports, and the Node bundles are ordinary bundled ESM without client directives. The browser TypeScript output is also unmarked. A Vite browser bundle or successful traditional server render is not an RSC qualification.

**Probe limit and contract recommendation.** No `next` or `react-server-dom-webpack` installation exists in the workspace or in the previously packed consumer dependency graph, and no framework-specific RSC fixture is present. Installing framework/RSC dependencies or changing production output is outside this report-only authorization. No RSC consumer probe was run. Recommendation: **Option B** — RSC applications must establish their own client boundary. Do not claim direct import/use of the package root or component subpaths from an RSC server graph as supported. A consumer should import the chosen Cyber Sheet UI from a module beginning with `'use client'`; it should construct the non-serializable `Workbook` within that client boundary (or pass serializable initialization data and construct it there). This is a contract recommendation, not a tested Next.js integration. It requires no package output changes now. If the project instead chooses Option A, directive-preserving entrypoints/bundling and framework integration would be a separate implementation decision.

For Option B, the minimum future qualification is a packed-consumer test in a pinned RSC framework: (1) build and install the exact packed React/Core/renderer artifacts; (2) have a server component import a consumer-owned `'use client'` wrapper and verify the framework recognizes the boundary; (3) create a Workbook inside the client wrapper and verify browser hydration, renderer identity, CSS loading, and disposal; (4) ensure the server component does not serialize/pass a Workbook instance through the Flight payload; and (5) document that direct package import from the server component graph and spreadsheet-grid server rendering are unsupported. If direct package imports are later promised, add a separate positive and negative framework test proving that each exported client entry is preserved as a client reference in the final package output.

**Exact scope.** Reviewed the existing FindService module record and the seven remaining semantic keys: `9179dda3478b114718cd`, `6ff6f36954972bd467d3`, `37261cb658d68cf23eea`, `a1f885ea7207e15bb9b7`, `7ab14a3361826a361d74`, `4d909820c9b99bc42e8c`, and `a17f39037c36dd892c27`. No implementation-ledger or frozen-register row was changed; the module and all seven semantics remain open.

**Source contract and result ownership.** `packages/core/src/index.ts` publicly re-exports `FindService`, `FindResult`, and `FindServiceOptions`. The constructor accepts `Worksheet | WorkbookSheetView`, and the service retains that exact source. The first-party `ExcelApp → FindReplaceDialog → FindService` route passes `workbook.activeSheet`, a `WorkbookSheetView`; standalone Worksheet construction remains part of the exported type. The dialog consumes result count and addresses, forwards only an address to ExcelApp, and does not retain `FindResult` objects in React state. No repository README/API guide documenting object-identity or standalone-vs-owner-view guarantees was found. The exported `FindServiceOptions` also declares `searchWithin` and `searchBy`, while `buildSearchOptions()` consumes `searchOrder` and does not read those two fields; the first-party dialog maps its `searchBy` state into `searchOrder`. Their external semantics remain unspecified in this review.

`WorkbookSheetView.findAll()` returns a detached address array, and its cell reads return detached snapshots with cached formula values masked or value searches rejected when formula caches could affect matches. FindService then stores each address in a new `FindResult`, but stores the returned result array as `lastResults` and returns that same array. Each result's `address` is the same object held internally. `findNext()`, `findPrevious()`, and `getCurrentMatch()` return the same internal result object. Therefore the values originate in a detached owner-view observation, but the service's public result array, result objects, and nested address objects are mutable aliases of FindService-local navigation state.

This is a concrete mutable service-state alias with a consequence on the explicitly supported standalone path: a caller can redirect a later `replaceCurrent()` target by mutating a previously returned address. It does **not** provide a Workbook/Worksheet capability or bypass an owner guard. For a WorkbookSheetView, replacements reject before using the result; for a raw Worksheet after internal adoption, the captured owner preflight rejects before returning or using service results. Mutating a detached result's strings/address does not mutate Workbook storage by itself.

**Public method and state transition matrix.**

| Method / transition | Current state behavior | Result/reference behavior and boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `findAll(nonempty)` succeeds | Saves new `lastOptions`, replaces `lastResults`, sets index to 0 or -1, returns `lastResults`. | Returned array, results, and nested addresses alias the service state. Owner-view source data remains detached from Workbook; standalone source works. |
| `findAll('')` | Clears results/options and sets index to -1 before returning a fresh empty array. | Existing previously returned arrays remain retained externally and are not revoked. |
| `findAll(nonempty)` throws during Worksheet/view search | `lastOptions` has already changed; the previous `lastResults` and `currentIndex` remain. | Failed-search state can pair the prior result with the new options. On the first-party owner view, a formula-sensitive value search may throw here. Replacement on the view still rejects; a custom standalone subclass that throws could expose the state mismatch. This is a source-derived state-consistency concern, not an observed owner-state disclosure. |
| `findNext()` / `findPrevious()` | Mutates `currentIndex` and returns the indexed internal object; empty results return null. | Same object identity as an entry of the returned `findAll()` array. Mutating it changes later navigation output. |
| `getCurrentMatch()` / count / index | Returns the current internal object, or scalar count / 1-based index (zero when empty). | Current-match object is aliased. Existing adopted-raw preflight rejects these calls after adoption; `clear()` is separately available. |
| `replaceCurrent()` | Uses `current.address` for the cell read; successful standalone replacement writes, splices the current internal array, and adjusts index. No-match/no-change paths return false. | Mutated result address can redirect the standalone target. Successful splice also changes the previously returned aliased array. Owner-view and adopted-raw branches reject before these operations. |
| `replaceAllMatches()` | Empty query returns 0 without changing state. Otherwise it performs standalone search/replacements, then clears `lastResults`, resets index, and saves the options. | Existing returned arrays remain externally retained snapshots of their prior entries, but their entries may already have been caller-mutated. Owner-view and adopted-raw paths reject before search/write. |
| `clear()` | Replaces service-local results with an empty array, resets index/options; no Worksheet method is called. | Legitimately callable after adoption; it cannot mutate Workbook state and does not erase arrays/objects already retained by callers. |

The first-party dialog passes `firstMatch.address` / navigation `match.address` to `onMatchSelected`. ExcelApp uses that plain address for selection state and renderer navigation. This does not forward a Worksheet or FindResult capability. No in-place address mutation was found in the traced first-party selection handling. ### P1-04G FindService residual authority and keyed closure review — 2026-10-24

**Public API versus JavaScript reflection.** The supported FindService methods retain their P1-04C adopted-raw preflight. A service constructed with the first-party `WorkbookSheetView` continues to reject replacement before invoking view methods. P1-04F additionally detaches every public result observation from the service's stored navigation/replacement objects.

TypeScript `private` is not runtime privacy. A disposable Jest probe used `Reflect.get(service, 'lastResults')` on a standalone service, changed its first internal address from A1 to B1, then called the supported `replaceCurrent('changed')`; B1 changed and A1 remained unchanged. A second probe constructed a service with a raw Worksheet, adopted the sheet through the internal helper, and confirmed `Reflect.get(service, 'worksheet')` returned that exact adopted Worksheet. The public `service.findAll('777')` rejected, while `Reflect.get(service, 'worksheet').getCell({row: 1, col: 1})` returned the stored cached value `777`. Thus reflection can alter internal replacement targets on a standalone service and can retrieve a retained raw source; the direct raw read is outside FindService's public method boundary. For the adopted-raw test, the caller created the service with that Worksheet and the adoption helper is internal; this is not a supported first-party Workbook ingress or a newly demonstrated first-party UI path.

A separate disposable probe exercised the first-party owner-view shape. `OwnerBackedWorkbookSheetView.getCellValue({row: 1, col: 1})` returned `null` for a formula cell, while reflective invocation of the prototype's TypeScript-private `sheet()` method returned the underlying adopted Worksheet and its cached `777` value. The reflected call path is `Reflect.get(Object.getPrototypeOf(view), 'sheet')` → `Reflect.apply(accessor, view, [])` → raw Worksheet. The view's `#resolve` field is ECMAScript-private, but its raw-returning `sheet()` method is not. This is a reflection-only capability exposure in the adjacent owner-view implementation, not a bypass through FindService's supported public methods. It is the concrete residual authority path required to stop this review; no correction was made under this report-only authorization.

**First-party consumer and identity compatibility.** `ExcelApp` passes `workbook.activeSheet` to `FindReplaceDialog`. The dialog keeps `FindService` in its component-local `findServiceRef`, reconstructing it when the `worksheet` prop identity changes. ExcelApp uses the address fields for selection and renderer navigation; it does not compare result arrays or result objects by identity. Repository searches of FindService consumers and the Find & Replace guide found value/address use and no identified first-party dependency on result-array or result-object reference equality. P1-04F's identity change is therefore covered by current first-party usage; undocumented external identity expectations remain a compatibility assumption, not a discovered caller dependency.

**Owner-view accessors and compatibility.** `OwnerBackedWorkbookSheetView` retains its resolver in the ECMAScript-private `#resolve` field (`packages/core/src/WorkbookSheetView.ts:45-51`). Its `sheet()` method at lines 53-57 is only TypeScript-private: reflective invocation through the instance prototype returns the raw `Worksheet`. `assertNoFormulaValuesInFilters()` at lines 59-71 is also TypeScript-private, but returns no Worksheet or data; it is an internal guard helper. Source search found no caller of either method outside this class. All view implementation methods use `this.sheet()` internally. The exported `WorkbookSheetView` interface (`packages/core/src/workbook-access-types.ts:34-77`) does not declare either member, and `OwnerBackedWorkbookSheetView` is not re-exported from the Core package root. Converting these implementation helpers to ECMAScript-private methods would not change that interface or its declaration contract.

**Ordinary public Workbook lifecycle.** `Workbook.create()` adopts every initial sheet before publishing it (`packages/core/src/workbook.ts:88-123`), and `getSheet()`/`activeSheet` return the cached owner view (`workbook.ts:487-493`). A disposable runtime probe called `Workbook.create({sheets:[{name:'Public'}]})`, reflectively invoked the view prototype's `sheet()`, and recovered the raw Worksheet. Both the owner view and raw handle returned `null` for the initially empty A1. `Reflect.get(view, '#resolve')` returned `undefined`, consistent with ECMAScript privacy. This ordinary initial-sheet path demonstrates raw-reference retrieval, but not successful state mutation or cached-formula disclosure.

**Additional dev-import path; stop condition reached.** The source contains two `@internal`, TypeScript-public Workbook methods. `createDevImportWorksheet()` returns a raw Worksheet and explicitly leaves it unadopted to permit import writes (`packages/core/src/workbook.ts:435-446`); `attachDevImportSheet()` places that sheet in Workbook registries without adopting it (`workbook.ts:448-468`). A subsequent raw `setCellValue(B1, 'mutated after attachment')` succeeded; the owner view then returned that new value for B1. This establishes a cached-value disclosure and post-attachment owner-state mutation path through the reflective accessor plus the internal dev-import seam. Per the directive's stop condition, no further capability probing or remediation work was performed.

The XLSX loader's only inspected source callers of these helpers are below the unconditional false R6 gate in `packages/io-xlsx/src/index.ts:18-21, 39-41, 112-159`; current public loader entrypoints reject before reaching them. The dev-import helpers nevertheless exist as callable methods in Core source and are explicitly marked `@internal`, so this probe is evidence about an internal seam, not a supported first-party Workbook mutation contract. The new Core regressions verify the attached candidate is owned before `getSheet()` can return a view, formula results remain masked, retained raw writes reject, and a cross-Workbook adoption failure leaves the receiving Workbook's names and views unchanged. No unadopted sheet was found registered through this helper after P1-04I. The adoption-failure case occurs before any registry write. The method has no rollback block for a hypothetical exception after the registry insertion while observer/bridge wiring runs; no such throwing path was identified or characterized here, so this remains a narrow failure-cleanup limitation rather than a reproduced partial publication.

Both public XLSX loaders still reject before parsing, Workbook construction, helper invocation, or publication (`packages/io-xlsx/src/index.ts:18-21, 28-42`). ### P1-04P Clipboard ownership and diagnostics contract decision — 2026-10-24

**Decision status.** This is a report-only contract decision. Approve fail-closed handling for adopted raw Worksheets at clipboard data-access boundaries; preserve standalone Worksheet behavior and read-only, formula-masked WorkbookSheetView Copy. Keep WorkbookSheetView Cut/Paste unavailable under current R2/R5 restrictions. Approve structural-only routine diagnostics: cell values and formula text/results must not be emitted in logs or error details. These decisions update the proposal status in this reconciliation record only; they do not edit the separate memo, implement behavior, promote ledger rows, or enable a later-slice write.

**Chosen compatibility contract.**

| Input/operation | R1 contract decision | Compatibility and evidence boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standalone `Worksheet` Copy, Cut, and Paste helper use | Preserve existing standalone behavior. Cut remains snapshot staging; it does not itself clear source cells. | Existing standalone Copy/Cut staging and replacement controls are distinct from Workbook-owned behavior. Successful standalone Paste completion is not established by the retained-raw tests and is not newly claimed here. |
| `WorkbookSheetView` Copy | Permit the owner-backed read path and a snapshot detached from Workbook storage. Copy may include formula text where the selected mode carries formulas; it must not include cached formula results. Plain-text/value projections use the view's masked `getCellValue()`. | First-party ExcelApp/HomeTab/Ribbon Copy supplies the active view. Focused Copy tests record owner-view masking and snapshot behavior. “Detached” means no cell/style object alias back into the Workbook; it does not promise recursively immutable clipboard payload objects to every external caller. |
| `WorkbookSheetView` Cut/Paste | Keep both unavailable before clipboard reads/staging, target reads, command construction, writes, or completion effects. | `performCut()` and `performPasteAsync()` reject the view at their current helper preflight. No R2 cell-content or R5 metadata/structure mutation is authorized. |
| Adopted raw `Worksheet` supplied to Copy/Cut/Paste helpers or clipboard services | Fail closed before reading cell contents, staging a payload, logging cell contents, or attempting system clipboard publication. Preserve the same operations for a genuinely standalone Worksheet. | Adoption does not revoke a caller's retained raw reference. This policy governs operation through these clipboard APIs after adoption; it does not promise that the raw reference itself is erased or converted into a view. |
| Owner-backed formula values | Never publish a cached formula result through a WorkbookSheetView clipboard projection. Formula text may be included by formula/all modes; displayed-value and plain-text projections remain masked. | This maintains the existing distinction between formula identity and cached-result visibility. It does not qualify formula freshness or enable R3 behavior. |
| Clipboard publication | Treat `ClipboardService` payload creation as internal staging; `navigator.clipboard.writeText()` invocation as attempted publication; a test spy observing its argument as mock-boundary evidence; only a resolving real browser/OS clipboard operation as confirmed external transfer. | The retained-raw Cut test observes staged cached data and a `writeText` call with the sentinel; its mock rejects and the helper absorbs the rejection. No successful external clipboard transfer is claimed. |
| Routine diagnostics and errors | Do not include cell values, formula text, cached results, or cell-derived payload contents. Structural diagnostics may include range, dimensions, counts, mode, and boolean presence flags. Errors should identify the denied operation/boundary without embedding cell data. | Source currently logs value/formula-bearing `captureDetails` and payload data in ClipboardService, and cell snapshot values in PasteCommand. These diagnostic paths are independent of whether a browser clipboard write succeeds. |
| Unsupported/later-slice entrypoints | Keep synchronous `performPaste()` and direct PasteCommand use from enabling owner writes; keep XLSX restoration and progressive import behind R6; retain R2/R5 restrictions. | `performPaste()` has no production caller located and is absent from the React root barrel. The exported Core PasteCommand still has target-read/log behavior in its constructor; this review does not accept it as an owner-write route. |

**Frozen-key scope and source trace.** The exact existing records relevant to this decision are:

| Boundary | Exact frozen keys | Source/evidence relation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clipboard wrapper ownership discriminator | Semantic `97f74ef69bf5289d4e0c` | `requireStandaloneWorksheet()` checks only for a `workbookId` property; this recognizes WorkbookSheetView shape but not private Worksheet adoption state. |
| Copy helper and first-party callers | Flows `110d0fa9b80dc8294f0f`, `c8ae56ede5c1cf32dd6d`, `342cc48e7b91de29f044`, `bf5997848c52927af634` | `performCopy()` has no ownership preflight; it stages through ClipboardService then may read plain text and call `writeText`. ExcelApp keyboard and Ribbon callers supply `workbook.activeSheet`; ClipboardGroup Copy has the same view path. |
| Cut helper and first-party callers | Flows `9b76ad9828df3e8123a2`, `4c685ba670d783ef2052`, `c527e914988bdaa9d662`, `289ea8864d96f7c12faf` | The wrapper's structural check precedes reads for a view. An adopted raw Worksheet lacks `workbookId`, passes the check, reaches snapshot staging and then plain-text clipboard publication. |
| Paste helper and first-party callers | Flows `c9f6edeac6ede11aa788`, `58adea2e127f7a8bbf19`, `fe29cf47a6ac21f9e72c`, `a8bec3be5dcab6730368`, `e165e1da47de6262e80f`, `cbd3e633229fb1981775` | Async helper rejects WorkbookSheetView before `getPayload()` or `readText()`, but the structural check does not reject an adopted raw Worksheet. Synchronous helper has no ownership preflight and no production caller was found. |
| ClipboardService snapshot reads/staging | Semantics `50be4fbb95e3d286dbec`, `f9288a29ff90a5317fa5`, `a61b814a55bdbb0c6d37`; flows `f0b0133fe720a75132f1`, `b09ccbe95bd29c5dbff5`, `d537f3ad20f5516fc65e`, `93f813839e362647de29`, `a8573467907939b9ac0e` | Exported Core `ClipboardService.copy()`/`cut()` call `createSnapshot()` without an ownership check. The snapshot is detached from cell/style objects, but read/logs cell values and the resulting payload retains cell contents. |
| PasteCommand target reads and diagnostics | Semantics `339942d8bc6975a6a327`, `a7fcd2afc449ff512f78` | Constructor/capture-state reads target merge and cell snapshots and logs target `value` before `CommandManager.execute()`. Retained-raw async Paste was intercepted at the manager boundary; retained-raw synchronous Paste reached execution and rejected on the tested `clearDependencies()` call, with cell/history/events unchanged. |

The lists above identify existing frozen records only; no identifiers were created or remapped. The four affected module records remain open. The first-party ExcelApp route passes a complete owner-backed active-sheet view. ClipboardGroup success callbacks run after helper success, so Cut's synchronous owner-view rejection precedes its local “clipboard has content” state and callbacks; async Paste's `.then()` callback is fulfillment-only. Its rejection presentation remains a separate UI requirement. `ExcelRibbon` has a direct-source exported component with a `Worksheet` prop and its own ClipboardService, but it is absent from the React root and ribbon barrels and no repository production caller was found. Direct-source/deep-import compatibility is therefore unresolved; no supported `ExcelRibbon` Workbook ingress was established.

**Earliest-check and publication assessment.** `performCopy()` currently has no ownership check. It calls `ClipboardService.copy()` (which reads, logs, and stores a snapshot) before it computes plain text and may invoke `navigator.clipboard.writeText()`. `performCut()` first calls `requireStandaloneWorksheet()`: the owner view is rejected there before snapshot reads/staging/publication, but an adopted raw Worksheet passes because ownership is private. The P1 retained-raw Cut test confirms staging plus a `writeText` spy call containing the cached-value sentinel; the Promise rejects, so actual external transfer is unproven. No Worksheet event is generated by staging or clipboard publication; Cut does not mutate the source.

There is a same-family lower-level contract gap: exported Core `ClipboardService.cut(view, range)` accepts a WorkbookSheetView directly and currently creates/stores an `isCut` snapshot because the service has no owner-operation check. It performs no Worksheet mutation or system clipboard write itself, so this is Cut staging rather than source clearing or confirmed publication. The chosen contract disallows even this owner-view Cut staging; a future guard must therefore cover the Core service, not only the React wrapper. `ClipboardService.copy(view, ...)` remains the explicitly permitted owner-view snapshot path.

`performPasteAsync()` checks the view-shaped `workbookId` property before internal `getPayload()` or external `navigator.clipboard.readText()`. For a retained raw adopted Worksheet, the check passes; internal Paste then constructs PasteCommand, whose merge/cell reads and diagnostic value capture precede command-manager execution. External-text Paste has the same target-snapshot boundary after the browser read. The async retained-raw test intercepted `CommandManager.execute()`, so that test proves pre-execution reads/logging, not successful mutation. Synchronous `performPaste()` has no preflight; its characterized internal-payload path reads the payload and reaches target snapshot/logging and the command, then rejects at the first tested owned mutator without cell changes, events, or history. The owner-view first-party paths reject before these effects. No new successful Workbook write or external clipboard transfer was found in this review.

The copied `requireStandaloneWorksheet` discrimination is not authoritative for retained raw Worksheets. A captured runtime method can enforce the selected policy for actual `Worksheet` instances without changing ordinary standalone behavior: capture `Worksheet.prototype.isWorkbookOwned` from the same Core package instance and call it directly on a recognized Worksheet before any cell access, staging, or publication; reject when owned, and keep the standalone result false. The view is classified separately: allow only its read-only Copy path and reject Cut/Paste. Treat failure to perform a trustworthy class/ownership check as rejection rather than falling through. This remains a feasibility conclusion, not an implementation. Duplicate Core package instances, proxies without the Worksheet private-field brand, and arbitrary structural objects are not established as supported inputs and need an explicit compatibility decision if required.

**Diagnostics decision and smallest follow-up.** The clipboard memo's proposed separation is accepted: prevent adopted raw sources from reaching clipboard reads/staging/publication, and independently redact value-bearing routine diagnostics. A wrapper-only guard is insufficient because Core `ClipboardService.copy/cut` are exported and do not call the React helper; direct construction/use of exported `PasteCommand` also reaches target snapshot logs. The smallest defensible production boundary for a future separately authorized correction is therefore: (1) a captured ownership preflight in the Core ClipboardService snapshot entry before reads/logs/staging, shared by copy and cut while allowing WorkbookSheetView only for Copy; (2) matching adopted-raw preflight in the React helper entrypoints, including `performCopy`, `performCut`, both Paste helpers, before system clipboard or target operations; (3) reject owner-backed Cut/Paste and keep all Workbook writes disabled; and (4) redact cell value/formula fields from ClipboardService and PasteCommand logs, preserving structural counts/ranges. Cover standalone Worksheet controls, formula-masked WorkbookSheetView Copy, adopted raw rejection with zero read/stage/writeText/log-content observations, owner-view Cut/Paste rejection, and diagnostic redaction. No portion of this correction is authorized by P1-04P.

Diagnostic evidence is independent of the clipboard-write mock: the retained-raw Cut test spies on `console.log` and asserts the cached sentinel occurs in ClipboardService's “Snapshot created” diagnostic; the async and synchronous retained-raw Paste tests separately inspect PasteCommand's “Captured snapshots” log and assert the target sentinel is present. The Cut test also asserts `writeText` receives the sentinel, but that is publication-boundary evidence, not the basis for the diagnostic decision.

**Decision and unresolved requirements.** The adopted-raw policy is fail-closed, and standalone compatibility is preserved. Owner-view Copy remains permitted but only with detached, formula-cache-masked data. Owner-view Cut/Paste remain rejected pending their journal-backed R2/R5 boundaries. Routine diagnostics must omit cell-derived data. No direct raw reference is said to be revoked. Remaining compatibility questions are external callers of the exported Core ClipboardService/PasteCommand, whether direct-source `ExcelRibbon` is a supported consumer API, and how first-party UI should communicate rejected Cut/Paste. The policy memo is now decisioned by this report, but the broader four module records and exact semantic/flow dispositions remain open.

No additional ownership escape outside the already reviewed clipboard family was established. P1-04P changes only this reconciliation report. No tests/builds, ledger changes, or frozen-register changes were made. `git diff --check` passed after this report-only update. Overall CS-002D4-R1 acceptance remains withheld; R2–R6 implementation, merge, release, reset, and baseline recapture remain unauthorized.

### P1-04Q Clipboard entrypoint and diagnostic-evidence review — 2026-10-24

**Review boundary.** Source-only review of the exported Core clipboard APIs, React helper entrypoints, first-party Ribbon callers, the retained-raw Cut/Paste characterizations, and their exact frozen records. No tests or builds were run; implementation and disposition changes remain unauthorized.

**Entrypoint matrix.**

| Entry point | Earliest current behavior | Ownership/effect finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ClipboardService.copy(worksheet, range, mode)` | Calls `createSnapshot()` before assigning `currentPayload`. Snapshot creation logs range metadata, reads cells or values, then logs and stores the detached payload. | No ownership preflight. WorkbookSheetView Copy is the permitted path: its `getCell()` returns detached cells with formula cached values masked, while `getCellValue()` masks formula results. An adopted raw Worksheet can pass the union type and expose its underlying cell value/formula. Core service staging changes only its own `currentPayload`; it does not mutate the Worksheet or publish to the browser clipboard. |
| `ClipboardService.cut(worksheet, range, mode)` | Same snapshot/read/log sequence, with `isCut: true`, followed by `currentPayload` assignment. | No ownership preflight. Direct `cut(WorkbookSheetView, ...)` currently stages an `isCut` payload even though the React helper rejects owner-view Cut. This is an internal clipboard-state change, not source-cell clearing or system-clipboard publication. The service has no `paste()` method; `getPayload()`, `clear()`, and `createPayloadFromPlainText()` do not read a Worksheet. |
| React `performCopy()` | Calls Core `copy()` first; unless disabled by options, then calls `payloadToPlainText()` and invokes `navigator.clipboard.writeText()`. | No guard. A retained adopted raw Worksheet can be read, staged, and passed to the system clipboard write boundary. The owner-view route is allowed for Copy, and both snapshot and plain-text reads use the view's detached/masked API. |
| React `performCut()` | Calls `requireStandaloneWorksheet()` before Core staging or plain-text serialization. | The helper rejects a `WorkbookSheetView` because it has `workbookId`, but this is a structural check, not an adopted-Worksheet check. The retained-raw fixture lacks that property and passes. It then stages a cut payload and attempts `writeText`; no source Worksheet mutation occurs at this helper stage. |
| React `performPasteAsync()` | Calls the same structural `requireStandaloneWorksheet()` before `getPayload()` or `navigator.clipboard.readText()`. | Owner views reject before clipboard/payload/target access. An adopted raw Worksheet passes the property check; internal payload then reaches `PasteCommand`, while external text is read and parsed before reaching the same command path. |
| React `performPaste()` | Reads `clipboardService.getPayload()` before constructing `PasteCommand`; it has no ownership preflight. | No production caller was found, and it is not re-exported from the React package root. A direct utility/deep-module caller with a retained raw Worksheet reaches target snapshot reads/logs before command execution. The tested execution later rejects at `clearDependencies()` before the tested target cell changes; this is not proof of general transaction atomicity. |
| Exported Core `PasteCommand` | Constructor stores the supplied Worksheet and payload, logs payload cell values/formulas, then `captureState()` reads merge/cell state and logs captured values. | Constructor has no owner guard. Direct construction with an adopted raw target can observe/log target state before execution. `execute()` later reaches Worksheet's guarded `clearDependencies()` before writes in the tested case. The direct constructor and command lifecycle remain public through Core exports, so React-only guards cannot enforce the full contract. |

**First-party and alternate callers.** ExcelApp keyboard Copy/Cut and keyboard/context-menu Paste use `workbook.activeSheet` (a WorkbookSheetView) and call the React helpers. The HomeTab `ClipboardGroup` receives the same view and shared ExcelApp ClipboardService: Copy succeeds and enables its local Paste button; Cut rejects before its success callbacks; Paste calls `performPasteAsync()` and rejects before payload/system reads or command construction. Its `.then()` callbacks are fulfillment-only and the handler has no local rejection presentation, so the source establishes no user-facing explanation for the disabled owner operation. The source-level `ExcelRibbon` component creates its own ClipboardService and passes its `Worksheet`-typed prop to ClipboardGroup. Although `ExcelRibbon` and `ClipboardGroup` are absent from the React root/ribbon barrels, `examples/react-canvas-viewer.tsx` directly imports `ExcelRibbon` and passes `workbook.getSheet(...)` to its `worksheet` prop; that is a first-party example call with a WorkbookSheetView at runtime. It confirms owner-view reachability through this deep-source route, while package-root support remains unestablished. Standalone Worksheet behavior remains a separate required compatibility control.

**Staging, publication, mutation, and diagnostics are distinct.** The retained-raw Cut test observes a Core `isCut` payload containing the cached formula value and confirms no Worksheet event or cell change. It separately observes `navigator.clipboard.writeText()` called with that value; the mocked Promise rejects and the helper absorbs the rejection. This proves attempted publication at the mock boundary, not successful browser/OS clipboard transfer. The async retained-raw Paste test intercepts `CommandManager.execute()` after PasteCommand construction, so it establishes target reads and logging but no command execution or write. The sync retained-raw test executes the command and observes rejection at `clearDependencies()`, with no cell change, event, or history addition. No successful Workbook mutation or external clipboard transfer is established.

The characterized value/formula-bearing diagnostic expressions are:

- `ClipboardService.createSnapshot()`: `captureLog` entries assign `logEntry.value = snapshot.value` in values, merge-anchor, and ordinary-cell branches (live lines 329, 374, 393); the “Snapshot created” log includes `captureDetails` and maps payload cells to `{ value: c.value, formula: c.formula }` (lines 417–425). The retained-raw Cut test asserts the cached-value sentinel appears in this log.
- `PasteCommand` constructor/capture: constructor logging maps payload cells to `value` and `formula` (lines 100–105); `captureState()` adds `captured.value = cell?.value` to each entry then logs `details` (lines 175–195). Both async and sync retained-raw Paste tests assert the sentinel appears in the “Captured snapshots” log. These diagnostics occur before the test's command-manager interception; the sync test separately confirms the later mutation guard.
- Additional PasteCommand execution logs are also value-bearing if execution progresses: `writeLog` stores `sourceValue`, `sourceFormula`, and `shiftedFormula`, then logs `details` (lines 331–368). They are not the source of the retained-raw rejected-path reproduction, but must follow the same routine-diagnostic rule.

Minimum redaction is to retain ranges, dimensions, offsets, counts, merge geometry, operation/mode, and presence booleans such as `hasValue`, `hasFormula`, and `hasStyle`, while removing cell values and formula text/results from all routine log objects and errors. This redaction is separate from the clipboard payload itself and from an intentional `writeText()` attempt. It must also preserve the approved owner-view Copy behavior without logging the formula text that Copy is allowed to retain in its internal payload.

**Earliest required guards.** Core `ClipboardService` needs an ownership/type preflight at the shared snapshot boundary before logging or reads, allowing WorkbookSheetView for Copy only and rejecting it for Cut; the exported Core API must independently reject adopted raw Worksheets for both operations. React helpers need matching guards at `performCopy`, `performCut`, `performPasteAsync`, and synchronous `performPaste`, before Core staging, clipboard reads/writes, or target access. `requireStandaloneWorksheet()` currently detects only the public `workbookId` shape, so it is insufficient for retained raw handles. Exported `PasteCommand` also needs a target ownership preflight in its constructor before snapshot reads/logs; the existing Worksheet mutator guard remains the last write boundary and must not be weakened. Preserve standalone Worksheet behavior and keep owner-view Cut/Paste disabled. If a trustworthy ownership check cannot classify an input, fail closed; do not fall through to structural compatibility.

### P1-04R Clipboard ownership enforcement and diagnostic redaction — 2026-10-24

**Implementation boundary.** Added preflight ownership classification at the Core ClipboardService snapshot boundary and the React helper boundaries. Each captures `Worksheet.prototype.isWorkbookOwned` from the Core runtime and invokes that captured predicate on actual Worksheet instances, so an instance shadow cannot disguise adopted ownership. A recognized standalone Worksheet remains valid for Copy/Cut/Paste. The separately recognized read-only WorkbookSheetView remains valid for Copy, while Cut and both Paste paths reject it. Adopted raw Worksheets and inputs that cannot be classified are rejected before worksheet reads, snapshot/payload replacement, system clipboard access, target capture, or command submission. Exported `PasteCommand` independently requires a standalone Worksheet before assigning command state, logging, or capturing target cells. No payload schema, owner-write permission, R2/R5 journal behavior, or Workbook mutation guard changed.

| Operation | Accepted input | Rejected-input boundary and observed effects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core `ClipboardService.copy()` | Standalone Worksheet; WorkbookSheetView | Adopted raw Worksheet rejects before reads, logs, or payload replacement. |
| Core `ClipboardService.cut()` | Standalone Worksheet | WorkbookSheetView and adopted raw Worksheet reject before reads, logs, or payload replacement. Direct owner-view Cut preserves a previously staged payload. |
| React `performCopy()` / `payloadToPlainText()` | Standalone Worksheet; WorkbookSheetView | Adopted raw/unknown input rejects before internal staging, cell reads, or `navigator.clipboard.writeText()`. |
| React `performCut()` | Standalone Worksheet | Owner view and adopted raw/unknown input reject before staging, reads, or browser clipboard invocation. |
| React `performPaste()` / `performPasteAsync()` | Standalone Worksheet | Owner view and adopted raw/unknown input reject before `getPayload()`, system clipboard reads, target reads, command history, events, or writes. |
| `new PasteCommand(target, ...)` | Standalone Worksheet | Owner view and adopted raw/unknown target reject before target capture, logging, or command execution. |

**Diagnostics.** Clipboard snapshot, PasteCommand constructor/capture, and execution logs now retain ranges, dimensions, offsets, merge geometry, operation labels, counts, and `hasValue`/`hasFormula`/`hasStyle` presence flags. Cell values, formulas, cached results, and payload contents are not placed in routine log objects. Redaction is separate from the detached ClipboardPayload and from permitted standalone system-clipboard publication; the payload shape and standalone behavior are unchanged. Sentinel regressions assert that value and formula strings do not occur in diagnostic calls. Execution logs now report `hasShiftedFormula` rather than formula text.

**Regression coverage.** Core ClipboardService tests cover standalone Copy/Cut, detached formula-masked WorkbookSheetView Copy, direct owner-view Cut without replacing an existing payload, adopted-raw Copy/Cut before reads/staging/logging, shadowed ownership methods, and diagnostic redaction. PasteCommand tests cover owner-view and adopted-raw constructor rejection before target reads/logs, redaction, and retained standalone execution/undo behavior. React clipboard suites cover owner-view Copy, rejection of owner-view Cut/Paste, adopted-raw Copy/Cut/async Paste/synchronous Paste preflight, preserved ClipboardService payload and command history, browser-clipboard non-invocation, and standalone Copy/Cut/Paste controls.

The nine pre-existing untracked generated JavaScript sidecars under `packages/core/src` were temporarily moved aside for each Jest selection so TypeScript source resolution was unambiguous, then restored by the command's exit trap. The tracked `packages/core/src/vanilla/ChartBuilder.js` was not moved. Final commands and results:

No arbitrary structural object or standalone Worksheet compatibility promise was established by the reviewed package contract.

**First-party rejection behavior.** A rejected owner Cut reaches `performCut()` synchronously from `ClipboardGroup.handleCut()` or ExcelApp's `cutSelection()` and throws before the handlers' success callbacks/state changes; the component does not catch it or show a user-facing explanation. The focused UI test captures the resulting `window` error. Owner Paste reaches `performPasteAsync()` and is rejected before payload lookup, but `ClipboardGroup.handlePaste()` attaches only a fulfillment continuation and ExcelApp's keyboard/context-menu paths discard the returned Promise. The existing regression wrapper explicitly consumes the rejection to avoid modeling browser `unhandledrejection`. Thus the source establishes a reachable rejected-operation error-handling defect/UX gap, separate from ownership safety: the operation fails closed, but first-party UI callers do not present the unavailable-operation reason and async callers can leave a rejected Promise unhandled. ### P1-04Y Ribbon ClipboardGroup Paste rejection containment — 2026-10-25

**Implementation.** Changed only `packages/react/src/components/ribbon/ClipboardGroup.tsx` for production behavior. `handlePaste()` now supplies a rejection callback directly to the Promise returned by `performPasteAsync()`. That branch returns without logging or rendering raw error content. `onPaste` and `onAfterClipboard` remain exclusively in the fulfillment callback, so rejection cannot trigger success callbacks or subsequent success effects. The Core owner-view guard and all Copy/Cut paths are unchanged. The component has no existing Paste-error presentation contract; rejection is contained without adding a prop, shared error infrastructure, or a new alert. The resulting user-visible limitation is that a rejected Ribbon Paste fails silently.

This correction supersedes P1-04X's earlier source-only finding that `ClipboardGroup.handlePaste()` left its `performPasteAsync()` rejection unhandled. That finding remains historical evidence for the pre-fix state; the current caller attaches the rejection branch described above.

Its actual ExcelApp Ribbon Copy→Paste test now returns the original rejected helper Promise unchanged; the wrapper stores only its Promise reference and does not attach a rejection handler or replace it with a fulfilled/pending Promise. The direct ClipboardGroup owner-view test likewise returns the original rejected Promise, with no test-side rejection consumer. Jest completes without an unhandled rejection, while assertions confirm the internal payload is unchanged, `getPayload()` and external `readText()` are not called during Paste, there are no owner/Worksheet reads, events, command executions or history changes, and no Paste success callbacks or pulse effects occur. ### P1-05F Cut retained-raw evidence reconciliation — 2026-10-25

**Historical observation and implementation phase.** The report's `Retained raw Worksheet Cut runtime characterization — 2026-10-23` records the pre-guard behavior. Its fixture made a standalone formula-bearing `Worksheet`, retained its raw reference, and adopted it through the internal `adoptWorksheetByWorkbook()` seam. In that implementation, React `requireStandaloneWorksheet()` rejected only objects with a `workbookId` property; the adopted raw Worksheet had no such property and passed. Core `ClipboardService.cut()` then built a snapshot, read/logged the cached formula result, and installed an `isCut` internal payload. React continued through `payloadToPlainText()` and invoked mocked `navigator.clipboard.writeText()` with the cached value. The mock rejected and the helper absorbed the rejection; the observation was an attempted write, not a successful browser/OS clipboard transfer. The source cell and formula remained unchanged and emitted no Worksheet event. This is historical evidence for the pre-guard implementation and an internal adoption seam, not a supported public Workbook lifecycle.

**Current source paths.** Current React `performCut()` calls `requireStandaloneWorksheet()` before mode resolution, `ClipboardService.cut()`, plaintext projection, or browser publication. The guard accepts a genuinely standalone `Worksheet`, but rejects both a `WorkbookSheetView` and a raw `Worksheet` whose captured Core ownership predicate reports adoption. Current Core `ClipboardService.createSnapshot()` independently calls `assertClipboardSourceAllowed()` before dimensions/logging/cell reads: it accepts a non-owned standalone Worksheet, rejects an adopted raw Worksheet using the captured `Worksheet.prototype.isWorkbookOwned`, and rejects a WorkbookSheetView for Cut. `ClipboardService.cut()` changes `currentPayload` only after snapshot creation succeeds. Thus current owner/adopted inputs reject before reads, diagnostic output, internal staging, or `writeText()`; the Core check is a second boundary for direct service callers.

For standalone Cut, React and Core checks permit the operation: Core reads and stages an immutable `isCut` payload, then the React helper projects plaintext and attempts `navigator.clipboard.writeText()`. Cut staging itself does not mutate the source Worksheet. The best-effort write helper catches a rejected browser Promise. For WorkbookSheetView, React rejects before Core; direct Core Cut independently rejects before snapshot work. For a retained raw adopted Worksheet, React rejects before Core and the Core service also rejects direct calls before snapshot work. `payloadToPlainText()` separately applies its Copy-source guard; it allows owner-view reads for Copy, but Cut cannot reach that projection for owner/adopted inputs because its earlier preflight rejects.

**Frozen identity and P1-05G evidence.** The unique frozen flow `4c685ba670d783ef2052` is type `worksheet-passed-to-call`, path `packages/react/src/utils/clipboardOperations.ts`, historical line `97`, expression `worksheet`, source anchor `void writeTextToSystemClipboard(payloadToPlainText(worksheet, range));`. **Complete `performCut()` publication route.** `performCut()` first applies `requireStandaloneWorksheet()`. For an allowed standalone Worksheet it then calls `ClipboardService.cut()`, which passes through Core `createSnapshot()` ownership validation, reads the selected cells, and updates the internal clipboard payload only after snapshot creation succeeds. If `writeSystemClipboard` is not explicitly false, the helper calls `payloadToPlainText()`; that function applies the Copy-source ownership validation, reads each selected `getCellValue()`, and joins cells with tabs and rows with newlines. The resulting text is sent to `writeTextToSystemClipboard()`, which calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText()` for nonempty text and absorbs a rejected Promise as best effort. Cut stages data but does not clear or otherwise mutate source cells; that later behavior is outside this call. An explicit `writeSystemClipboard: false` option skips the publication expression, but the default/ordinary helper path exercises it.

**Standalone Worksheet evidence.** The existing focused standalone helper control calls real `performCut()` on a standalone Worksheet with A1 populated and A1:B1 selected. The test's mock resolves; it demonstrates a staged payload and an attempted browser API write at the mock boundary. It does not establish that the browser or operating system actually transferred the text. Core ClipboardService standalone Cut coverage separately confirms snapshot staging. This is the standalone branch of the same owner-polymorphic helper occurrence, not evidence of a public React package-root API promise.

**WorkbookSheetView evidence.** In first-party ExcelApp keyboard/Ribbon routes, `workbook.activeSheet` is a WorkbookSheetView. `performCut()` rejects it at `requireStandaloneWorksheet()` before Core staging, plaintext projection, or `writeText()`. Existing ExcelApp owner-flow regressions verify no Core `cut()`, owner cell reads, publication, payload replacement, or success effects. Direct Core `ClipboardService.cut(view)` also rejects before snapshot work and preserves the existing payload. These owner-view paths do not imply that owner-backed Cut succeeds.

**Retained raw Worksheet evidence.** The October 23 characterization remains a historical pre-guard observation using the internal `adoptWorksheetByWorkbook()` seam: the raw handle passed the then-structural guard, staged a cached formula result, and reached mocked `writeText()`, whose Promise rejected. Under current source, React's `requireStandaloneWorksheet()` uses the captured Core ownership predicate and rejects the adopted raw Worksheet before `ClipboardService.cut()`. ### P1-05O ClipboardService remaining ownership-boundary evidence matrix — 2026-10-25

**Scope and method.** Report-only review of the one Core ClipboardService module row, all eight frozen semantic rows, and all five frozen flow rows for `packages/core/src/ClipboardService.ts`. Each frozen row was matched to the current ledger identity and disposition, then assessed against current `ClipboardService.ts`, `WorkbookSheetView.ts`, `Worksheet` read behavior, and existing Core/React clipboard regressions. No production source, tests, implementation-ledger rows, or frozen registers were changed. “Evidence sufficient” below is key-scoped and does not close the containing module or neighboring occurrence.

**Current entry contract and source findings.** `ClipboardService` is exported from the Core package root. Its `copy()` and `cut()` entrypoints accept the source union `Worksheet | WorkbookSheetView`; `createSnapshot()` calls `assertClipboardSourceAllowed()` before reading or logging. A direct Worksheet input is classified using `instanceof Worksheet` and a captured `Worksheet.prototype.isWorkbookOwned`, so an adopted raw Worksheet rejects even if its instance method is shadowed. A recognized WorkbookSheetView is accepted for Copy and rejected for Cut. Standalone Worksheet remains accepted for both. The service stores only the resulting `currentPayload`; it does not retain the source Worksheet or a callback after the synchronous snapshot call.

The first-party owner-view behavior is bounded: `OwnerBackedWorkbookSheetView.getCell()` returns detached data and masks formula cached values when formula identity is present; `getCellValue()` also masks formula cached values. ClipboardService preserves formula identity in `all` mode and reads through `getCellValue()` in `values` mode, where formula identity is intentionally omitted by the values-only projection. P1-04R and P1-05K tests cover owner-view and standalone Copy controls, direct adopted-raw Copy/Cut rejection before reads/staging/logging, source and payload preservation, diagnostic redaction, and the merged-anchor formula case. P1-05M directly qualifies the merge-query result. Existing tests do not establish every public adapter/structured-value contract described below.

**Source-established residual risk — structurally recognized facade.** The runtime `isWorkbookSheetView()` guard checks only that the value is an object with string `workbookId`/`worksheetId` and callable `getCell`, `getCellValue`, and `getMergedRangeForCell`; it does not establish that the object is an `OwnerBackedWorkbookSheetView` or another authorized Workbook-created view. Therefore an object facade around a retained adopted raw Worksheet can satisfy the guard. Exact path: `ClipboardService.copy(facade, range)` → `createSnapshot()` → `assertClipboardSourceAllowed()` takes the structural-view branch → `getMergedRangeForCell()` and `getCell()` (or values-mode `getCellValue()`) dispatch to facade methods. If those methods delegate to the adopted raw Worksheet, the `getCell()` path can put its cached formula value in the snapshot, and the values-mode path can copy it without formula identity; neither is passed through the genuine owner view's formula-masking methods. This is a source-established bypass mechanism for externally constructed structural facades, not a runtime reproduction and not a first-party route identified in this review. Existing adopted-raw tests pass the raw Worksheet directly and do not characterize this wrapper. Do not remediate or promote from this source-only observation; the focused characterization below should establish actual behavior and the intended structural-view contract first.

**Standalone and payload qualifications.** No raw Worksheet object is retained by the service. Separately, standalone `Worksheet.getCell()` returns a shallow frozen cell copy and standalone `getCellValue()` returns the stored value; for structured `RichTextValue`/`EntityValue` cells, `createCellSnapshot()` assigns `cell.value` directly and only freezes the outer cell snapshot. That source path can leave a nested structured value shared between the standalone source and clipboard payload; no focused structured-value alias test was found. This is a standalone payload-alias question, not an owner-backed Worksheet escape. Also, `sourceRange` freezes a shallow copy while retaining the input range's `start` and `end` address objects. These are detached-payload/compatibility limitations, not evidence that the service retains a Worksheet or that a genuine owner view discloses its cached formula result. The tested nested serialized style likewise remains mutable while detached from the owner style; it is not deeply immutable.

### P1-05P Structural facade cached-formula disclosure characterization — 2026-10-25

**Scope.** Added one characterization to `packages/core/__tests__/ClipboardService.test.ts`; no production source, implementation-ledger disposition, or frozen classification register was changed. The fixture creates a standalone Worksheet, gives it a distinctive cached formula result, adopts it through the existing internal `adoptWorksheetByWorkbook()` seam, then constructs a structural `WorkbookSheetView` facade whose IDs and three required methods satisfy `isWorkbookSheetView()` and delegate reads to the adopted raw Worksheet. The test exercises `ClipboardService.copy()` in `all` and `values` modes and compares the resulting payload with a genuine `OwnerBackedWorkbookSheetView` control.

**Runtime result.** The structural facade is accepted. In `all` mode, the payload contains cached value `structural-facade-cache-sentinel` together with formula `40+2`; in `values` mode, the payload also contains the sentinel and omits formula identity. The facade read counters establish the paths: the `all` copy calls its merge and cell methods once each and does not call `getCellValue()`; the `values` copy calls `getCellValue()` once. By contrast, the genuine owner-backed view's `all` payload preserves formula `40+2` but contains `null`, not the cached sentinel. This confirms a cached-formula disclosure through a caller-constructed structural facade, distinct from the genuine owner-view boundary. It does not establish that the facade is an intended or supported API contract.

The source cell's formula and cached value remain unchanged, its merge geometry is unchanged, and the Worksheet event listener observes zero events. Each successful Copy updates the service's current payload as expected; the previously returned seed payload remains unchanged after later copies. This is a synchronous clipboard snapshot disclosure, not retention of the raw Worksheet by `ClipboardService`, a source mutation, or a successful browser/system clipboard transfer.

**Source correlation.** `packages/core/src/ClipboardService.ts` `isWorkbookSheetView()` checks only object-ness, string `workbookId`/`worksheetId`, and callable `getCell`, `getCellValue`, and `getMergedRangeForCell`. `assertClipboardSourceAllowed()` accepts that structural branch for Copy without proving Workbook-issued view provenance. `createSnapshot()` then reads through the supplied methods: `getCell()` in `all` mode and `getCellValue()` in `values` mode. The facade delegates those reads to the adopted raw Worksheet, bypassing the formula-cache masking that the genuine owner view applies. The test therefore turns the P1-05O source mechanism into a focused runtime finding.

**Disposition and next decision.** Keep all ledger dispositions, including the two P1-05N promotions, unchanged. This characterization does not itself authorize or implement remediation. A separate bounded decision should determine the intended adapter contract and, if structural facades are not trusted inputs, authorize a provenance check at the ClipboardService boundary that preserves standalone Worksheet Copy and genuine owner-view Copy while rejecting an untrusted facade before delegated reads. The separate standalone structured-value alias and shallow `sourceRange` address concerns remain outside this finding.

### P1-05Q ClipboardService owner-view provenance decision — 2026-10-25

**Decision.** Adopt this R1 input invariant for ClipboardService: structural compatibility alone does not establish workbook-owned read authority. Copy may consume a WorkbookSheetView only when it is the exact view issued by a Workbook through its owner-view creation path. This decision follows the P1-05P runtime disclosure and is limited to the ClipboardService input boundary; it does not change the wider WorkbookSheetView interface or authorize implementation in this phase.

**Current construction and identity boundary.** `Workbook.#viewFor()` in `packages/core/src/workbook.ts` constructs an `OwnerBackedWorkbookSheetView` for the current workbook and worksheet IDs and caches that view in `#viewsById`; public `getSheet()` and `activeSheet` return that cached reference. The class in `packages/core/src/WorkbookSheetView.ts` has a JavaScript private `#resolve` field and is frozen after construction, but its constructor is exported from that internal source module and accepts caller-supplied IDs and a resolver. Thus neither `instanceof OwnerBackedWorkbookSheetView` alone nor the current structural interface check proves the particular instance came from `Workbook.#viewFor()`. Frozen own properties and the resolver's private-field encapsulation protect object behavior/state but do not establish issuer provenance. `WorkbookId` and `WorksheetId` use TypeScript `unique symbol` brands, which are compile-time distinctions and do not create runtime authentication.

The Core package root exports the `WorkbookSheetView` interface as a type but does not re-export the `OwnerBackedWorkbookSheetView` runtime class. The class remains importable by internal source modules and tests. This is evidence of the intended internal construction boundary, not a claim that callers with arbitrary same-process access to package internals are cryptographically isolated.

**Accepted compatibility matrix.**

| Input | P1-05Q contract | Required behavior at the clipboard boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact Workbook-issued owner view returned by `getSheet()` / `activeSheet` | Supported owner-backed Copy source | Accept; preserve detached reads and formula cached-value masking. |
| Standalone `Worksheet` not adopted by a Workbook | Existing compatibility path | Preserve current Copy and Cut behavior. |
| Adopted raw `Worksheet` passed directly | Rejected owner-storage handle | Reject before cell reads, payload replacement, or diagnostics. |
| Structural facade, including one delegating to an adopted raw Worksheet | Not an authorized owner view under this decision | Reject before invoking facade methods or publishing/replacing a payload. |
| Manually constructed `OwnerBackedWorkbookSheetView` not issued by a Workbook | Not an authorized owner view under this decision | Reject on provenance, even if its class and methods look genuine. |

**Provenance design constraint for P1-05R.** Establish the accepted identity at the single Workbook view-issuance boundary and have ClipboardService consult that authority; do not create a second definition based on IDs, method shape, a forgeable public symbol, or `instanceof`. An issuer-owned identity registry such as a private `WeakSet` is a candidate only if registration is confined to Workbook issuance through an internal construction capability that is not part of the package's public API. The next implementation design must account for the currently exported internal constructor: simply registering every constructed instance, or adding an exported `registerView()` callable by facades, would preserve the bypass. Keep standalone Worksheet classification independent from view provenance, and ensure rejection happens before any delegated reads, logs, or `currentPayload` replacement.

**Governance and next phase.** This is a report-only contract decision. No production source, tests, ledger rows/dispositions, or frozen registers changed in P1-05Q. P1-05N's two `implemented-detached-result` promotions remain unchanged; the 2,067-record ledger and all frozen registers remain outside this phase. P1-05R is the separately authorized next decision point for the smallest implementation and regression set; P1-05Q itself does not authorize those edits. No tests or typecheck were required. `git diff --check` was run after this report update and passed. Overall CS-002D4-R1 acceptance remains withheld.

### P1-05R Workbook-issued view provenance remediation — 2026-10-25

**Implementation.** `Workbook` now keeps issued view identities in a private static `WeakSet<object>`. Its private `#viewFor()` adds a view only when the Workbook constructs and caches it. A read-only `Workbook.isWorkbookIssuedSheetView()` predicate queries that registry; its property on the exported Workbook class is made non-writable and non-configurable. No method, symbol, or instance field grants registration. The existing `OwnerBackedWorkbookSheetView` constructor remains available from its internal module for compatibility with internal tests, but instances constructed directly are not registered.

`ClipboardService` preserves the direct Worksheet branch and its captured-prototype ownership check: standalone Worksheets remain usable, while adopted raw Worksheets reject before reads. For non-Worksheet inputs, it now accepts only an identity present in the Workbook registry; it no longer treats structural method/ID compatibility as authority. The check runs in `assertClipboardSourceAllowed()` before `createSnapshot()` emits diagnostics or performs delegated reads, and before `copy()`/`cut()` replaces `currentPayload`. Workbook-issued views still reach their detached, formula-masking reads; owner-view Cut remains rejected.

**Attack-path results.**

| Input/path | Before P1-05R | After P1-05R |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Structural facade delegating to an adopted raw Worksheet, `all` and `values` | P1-05P runtime reproduction exposed the cached sentinel in both modes. | Both calls reject with the Workbook-issued-view error before any facade method call, diagnostic log, or payload replacement. |
| Directly constructed `OwnerBackedWorkbookSheetView` with caller IDs/resolver | The prior structural guard would admit its shape; this exact instance path had not been separately runtime-tested before the fix. | Rejected by identity before its resolver is invoked; it cannot grant itself authority through constructor use. |
| Workbook-issued view | Existing behavior accepted structurally; genuine-view masking was demonstrated in P1-05P. | Accepted by registered identity; formula `40+2` is preserved and cached value remains `null`. |
| Standalone Worksheet | Existing Copy/Cut compatibility. | Preserved by the dedicated Worksheet branch and focused regression suite. |
| Retained raw Worksheet before and after Workbook adoption | Direct adopted-raw rejection was already established; transition behavior is now explicitly characterized. | The same raw reference copies while standalone, then rejects after `attachDevImportSheet()` adoption before cell reads or payload/log changes; its Workbook-issued view copies with the cached formula result masked. |

The regression also verifies that a rejected facade leaves an earlier stored payload current and unchanged, while later successful Copy replaces only the service's current payload and does not mutate the earlier detached result. The provenance query itself cannot be replaced through the Workbook constructor because its property is non-writable and non-configurable. The registry remains inaccessible and contains weak identities rather than mutable view fields.

**Prioritized residual gaps.**

1. **Structural owner-view facade accepted by CanvasRenderer — highest priority; source-established route, runtime characterization pending.** `WorkbookSheetView` is a TypeScript interface. `Workbook` brands only its actual views in a private `WeakSet`, and exposes the read-only `Workbook.isWorkbookIssuedSheetView()` predicate. In `CanvasRenderer`'s constructor, `sheet instanceof Worksheet` selects the observation Proxy; every other object is assigned directly to `#sheet`. No issued-view predicate is called. The renderer then reads `#sheet.getCellValue()` and supplies the result as `value` to plugin callbacks. Therefore a structural facade delegating to an adopted raw Worksheet can satisfy the TypeScript shape while returning the raw cached formula value; the source path has no provenance rejection. This is not yet runtime-reproduced, and the public structural typing does not itself settle a compatibility promise. Relevant keys: `e11a689e9d6c4221bc7a`, `f68d66f22807aa296e05`, `e00e049141e55ab4bac7`, `78ad5d4e630576e8448c`, and the exact render read `0eca20ea033bce6593ef`.
2. **Worker handoff across a reentrant adoption — source-level lifecycle gap, not yet characterized.** `hydrateFormulaWorker()` checks `isWorkbookOwned()` once, then synchronously enumerates cells and calls the externally supplied `FormulaWorkerBridge.setCellValue/setCellFormula` for each cell. The bridge method is caller code and may re-enter; if the first call adopts the retained Worksheet through the existing internal test seam, enumeration may continue and hand later non-formula values to the worker after ownership changed. Existing tests cover entry after adoption, adoption before async batch resolution/rejection, replacement hydration after adoption, and disposal generation, but not adoption re-entered from a bridge callback during a multi-cell hydration pass. Relevant keys: semantic `a66b6ef010c2ea6f9683`, flows `7c87c29f784578ff943e`, `5942673a7ba065dc2371`, and `c110b1a4062aab7b587f`. This internal-seam timing is lower priority than the structural facade path and is not treated as a confirmed disclosure.
3. **`onMutation()` subscription capability — retained but no current owner delivery path established.** The observation Proxy forwards this Worksheet-only method; tests establish standalone delivery/disposal, subscription registration through retained raw and renderer handles after adoption, and that tested adopted writes reject before notification. Worksheet owner-side mutation events are not reachable through the present R1 public mutation surface, so listener payload delivery, listener lifecycle under an owner event, exceptions/reentrancy, and ordering remain unverified rather than demonstrated as a current owner escape. The four handle keys above cover retention/exposure; no frozen record names `onMutation()` or its emitter directly. Ordering remains an R4 dependency.
4. **Plugin lifecycle and owner-view compatibility beyond provenance.** Supported plugin context data, style, and address snapshots are detached; a tested unchecked function-valued cell input is passed by identity but cannot mutate an adopted Worksheet through the tested guarded setter. Plugin registration/removal and callback retention across renderer disposal/session changes are not comprehensively reconciled. These remain separate from the selected facade disclosure and do not establish a new defect by themselves.

**P1-06B recommendation — one focused test-only characterization.** Use the existing renderer test harness and internal adoption seam; do not change production code in the characterization. Create a formula cell with a distinctive cached sentinel on a standalone Worksheet, adopt it, and pass CanvasRenderer a structural `WorkbookSheetView` facade whose read methods delegate to that raw Worksheet. Confirm the facade fails `Workbook.isWorkbookIssuedSheetView()` while a genuine Workbook-issued control passes. Add a RenderPlugin callback that captures `context.value`, trigger a real renderer redraw, and assert the desired owner boundary: the structural facade is rejected before cell reads or the formula sentinel reaches the plugin. Preserve separate controls for a genuine Workbook-issued view (masked cached value), an adopted raw Worksheet passed directly (observation Proxy masks), and standalone Worksheet compatibility. Record cell-read counts, plugin values, source state/events, and any partial rendering. Keep the assertion that rejects exposure even if the current implementation reproduces the leak; do not remediate in the characterization. This harness uses internal adoption only and does not establish a supported public raw-Worksheet adoption route. The result should decide whether a minimal provenance guard is warranted and which external structural compatibility, if any, needs a separate contract decision.

### P1-06B Structural WorkbookSheetView facade characterization — 2026-10-25

**Test-only characterization.** Added `packages/renderer-canvas/__tests__/renderer-structural-view-facade.r1.test.ts`. The test constructs a formula `=40+2` with cached sentinel `cached-owner-sentinel-40617`, adopts the raw Worksheet through the existing internal `adoptWorksheetByWorkbook()` seam, and builds a non-Worksheet structural facade whose delegated methods call the adopted raw Worksheet. `Workbook.isWorkbookIssuedSheetView(facade)` is false. The test exercises `CanvasRenderer`'s actual plugin-rendering callback and records read, callback, diagnostic, subscription, canvas, source-state, and event effects. It also includes genuine Workbook-issued-view, standalone Worksheet, and retained observation-handle-after-adoption controls.

**Observed boundary.** The structural facade is accepted. `CanvasRenderer` constructs successfully, reads through the facade, adds its canvas, and subscribes through `on()` without a diagnostic. Across the constructor redraw, plugin redraws, and explicit redraw, the delegated `getCellValue()` counter records 64 reads. On the measured redraw, the plugin callback runs 16 times; its A1 value capture observes the cached sentinel three times across three redraws. There is one delegated `on()` registration and, after `dispose()`, one matching disposer call. One canvas exists before disposal and the container has no children afterward. `console.warn` and `console.error` each remain at zero calls. The adopted source's cached sentinel is unchanged and its Worksheet event list remains empty. This is runtime-confirmed formula-cache disclosure to a rendering callback through an unissued facade, not a Worksheet mutation or a retained raw reference acquired from CanvasRenderer.

All 22 current ledger rows were confirmed `open-not-reconciled`; there are no EditingManager flow rows in the frozen flow register. The records remain unchanged pending a separate exact-key evidence-to-disposition review.

**Contract and correction.** EditingManager now has an explicit standalone-Worksheet input contract. The module captures `Worksheet.prototype.isWorkbookOwned` once and calls that intrinsic on the supplied Worksheet, so an instance-level `isWorkbookOwned() => false` shadow cannot bypass the ownership check. The constructor rejects adopted or non-authentic structural inputs before registering copy/cut/paste document listeners. Because a valid standalone Worksheet can be adopted later, copy, cut, paste, fill, command execution, undo, redo, and clear-history paths repeat the synchronous check at their entry boundary. This prevents formula-bearing cell reads, clipboard reads/writes, Worksheet writes, and undo/redo stack changes after adoption. The check is deliberately fail-closed: no WorkbookSheetView API was added. Listener teardown for a manager adopted after construction remains a separate lifecycle concern; its still-registered listener rejects before event cancellation, clipboard access, cell access, or publication.

**Historical pre-fix behavior.** The prior focused characterization observed cached formula result `42` in plain text, HTML, CSV, and custom clipboard payloads after adoption; Cut also published its clipboard payload before its Worksheet write was rejected. The fill control read the formula source and target before its rejected write. Undo then attempted its restore, failed at the owner write guard, and had already removed its command from undo history. These observations remain the pre-fix record; the updated passing assertions below establish the corrected boundaries.

**Regression evidence.** Updated the existing focused EditingManager owner-boundary regressions and added `editing-manager-standalone-contract.r1.test.ts`. The controls preserve standalone formula copy, cut, custom paste, fill branches, and paste undo/redo behavior.
