Each places distinct values and different styles in neighboring cells, checks both shift destinations after execute, checks original addresses and cleared destinations after undo, and verifies redo restores shifted values/styles. History sizes are asserted before execute, after execute, after undo, and after redo. These cases pass with the original `DeleteCellsCommand` and Worksheet implementation unchanged.

**AE.03 — Calculated-field null decision package.** The proposed named-value evaluator should preserve four distinct input states. Recommended rule for that *new explicit binding path* is to propagate explicit null through arithmetic, functions receiving the binding, and dependent calculated fields; keep absent declared values as `#REF!`, present zero as numeric zero, and spreadsheet Errors as their error code. This limits compatibility impact to the additive pivot-binding API. Ordinary Worksheet evaluation remains untouched: current `FormulaEngine` arithmetic applies JavaScript numeric operators to cell values, and `SUM` filters non-numeric inputs, so changing ordinary blank-cell behavior would be a separate compatibility change.

| Expression / input state | Propagate-null recommendation | Coerce-null-to-zero alternative | Spreadsheet-error alternative |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Revenue + 1`, Revenue is null / absent / zero / `#DIV/0!` | null / `#REF!` / 1 / `#DIV/0!` | 1 / `#REF!` / 1 / `#DIV/0!` | `#VALUE!` / `#REF!` / 1 / `#DIV/0!` |
| `SUM(Revenue)`, Revenue is null / absent / zero / Error | null / `#REF!` / 0 / same spreadsheet error code | 0 / `#REF!` / 0 / same spreadsheet error code | `#VALUE!` / `#REF!` / 0 / same spreadsheet error code |
| `Profit + 1`, where `Profit = Revenue - Cost` evaluated to null / absent / zero / Error | null / `#REF!` / 1 / same spreadsheet error code | 1 / `#REF!` / 1 / same spreadsheet error code | `#VALUE!` / `#REF!` / 1 / same spreadsheet error code |
| `Revenue - Cost`, with either operand absent versus explicitly null | `#REF!` if absent; null if either present operand is null | `#REF!` if absent; use zero for a null operand | `#REF!` if absent; `#VALUE!` for a null operand |

Propagation is recommended because it does not silently reinterpret an explicitly present null aggregate as zero and keeps it distinct from both absence and numeric zero. Function behavior for a null named argument must follow the same rule; ordinary cell/range `SUM` behavior is not changed. This recommendation is not an implementation authorization. The decision remains pending, including whether the product accepts the intentional difference between explicit named-null `SUM` and current Worksheet range-blank behavior.

**AE.04 — Numeric helper and OR observations.** Added independent reference-point checks without changing the existing failing assertions. Expected values use standard distribution definitions: Student-t and F tails/quantiles from regularized-beta calculations, chi-square with two degrees of freedom from `exp(-x/2)`, chi-square quantile reference for 10 degrees of freedom, and standard-normal CDF/PDF/quantile points. Direct mathematical helpers and public formula calls match within the encoded tolerances. For example, `T.DIST.RT(1.96,60)` is approximately `0.0273224649`; `F.DIST.RT(1,5,10)` approximately `0.4651194265`; `CHISQ.DIST.RT(5,2) = exp(-2.5)`; and `NORM.S.DIST(1,TRUE)` approximately `0.8413447461`. Thus the existing `#VALUE!` expectations are unsupported by these independent oracles; no product function defect is established.

For `OR(A1>60,B1<110)`, independently evaluating the two predicates gives false and true respectively. The compiled expression reads both cells (the resolver log is `B1`, then `A1`) and returns true for the combined expression. `OR(TRUE,FALSE)` also returns true, separating Boolean coercion from reference substitution. The original characterization still asserts false and therefore fails; the current observation does not support its “only first predicate” premise. No production FormulaEngine, function-library, or conditional-formatting source was changed, and the old assertion remains visible for a separately authorized correction.

### P1-08AG.01–AG.06 — Explicit named-value evaluation and pivot integration preparation — 2026-10-29

**AG.01 — Additive evaluator boundary.** Added `FormulaEngine.evaluateWithBindings(formula, worksheetContext, namedValues)` in `packages/core/src/FormulaEngine.ts`. It accepts the approved `ReadonlyMap<string, FormulaValue>` contract, validates ASCII identifiers (`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`), normalizes names to uppercase, and rejects case-insensitive duplicates before evaluation. The binding namespace is carried only by the explicit call; ordinary `evaluate()` retains its existing entrypoint and does not consult it. Binding lookup is a final bare-identifier fallback after Boolean literals, lambda locals/named lambdas, and cell/range references, while registered function-call parsing remains ahead of bare-name fallback. Invalid names and duplicate normalized names raise `TypeError` at the explicit API boundary.

The approved distinction between an unavailable declared name and an undeclared name is represented without widening `FormulaValue`: a declared name with no per-cell result is passed as an explicit `Error('#REF!')` map value, while a missing map key evaluates as `#NAME?`. A present numeric zero remains zero. Explicit named null uses a private internal marker so arithmetic, unary operators, `IF`, and registered function arguments such as `SUM(Revenue)` propagate null without changing ordinary empty-cell or range-function coercion. The marker is unwrapped before returning the public `FormulaValue`; spreadsheet Errors preserve their codes. Named bindings survive LET/lambda-derived evaluation contexts, with LET/lambda-local values retaining precedence. This API is an evaluator boundary only; no PivotCalculatedFieldEngine or PivotEngine production integration was made.

**AG.02–AG.03 — Regression contract and red/green evidence.** Added `packages/core/__tests__/formula-engine-named-bindings.p1-08ag.test.ts`. Before the evaluator implementation, the new test suite ran against the current source and failed 4 named-binding tests / passed 2 dependency-characterization tests because `evaluateWithBindings` did not exist. After implementation the six-test AG file passed. The test contract verifies explicit-only bare-name resolution, case-insensitive matching, A1 and range reads, `TRUE`, registered `SUM`, LET/lambda-local precedence, invalid and duplicate names, `#REF!` for an explicitly represented unavailable declared input, `#NAME?` for an undeclared input, zero, explicit-null propagation through arithmetic/function/IF paths, Error-code retention, and unchanged ordinary Worksheet blank-cell arithmetic and `SUM` behavior.

**AG.04 — Dependency integration characterization and design.** The new test confirms that `PivotCalculatedFieldEngine.compile()` currently preserves `Revenue` and `revenue` as distinct dependencies and `topologicalSort()` does not recognize a cycle when the calculated-field reference differs from its declaration only by case. The next integration should use the same ASCII, case-normalized namespace as the explicit evaluator: reject duplicate labels after normalization, exclude function names and A1/range tokens from dependency edges, normalize aggregate/calculated labels and references consistently, treat aggregates as graph roots, sort calculated-field nodes, and report cycles using the existing circular-dependency error contract. When a dependency is declared but has no value for one pivot cell, the adapter should pass `Error('#REF!')`; an identifier outside the compiled namespace should remain `#NAME?`. This is a design boundary, not a PivotCalculatedFieldEngine production change.

**AG.05 — Future pivot-cell integration boundary.** For each pivot cell, the future adapter should compute every configured aggregate independently and create one normalized label-to-value map. It should evaluate calculated fields in dependency order using the explicit API, adding each result to the map before evaluating dependent fields. Preserve `PivotCell.value` as the existing primary aggregate value and publish all aggregate and calculated labels through `PivotCell.values`; null and Error results remain per-field values and do not alter cell shape. First qualify this on the supported standalone pivot computation path. Workbook-owned registry publication remains a separate internal/owner-journal contract and requires its own authorization; this checkpoint adds no Workbook API or registry access.

### P1-08AH.01–AH.09 — Named-binding audit, standalone pivot integration, and R1 failure-family review — 2026-10-29

**AH.01/AH.05 — Independent evaluator audit and regression matrix.** Added `packages/core/__tests__/formula-engine-named-bindings.audit.p1-08ah.test.ts`; the seven tests pass. They verify per-call binding lifetime (ordinary `evaluate()` remains unbound before and after), nested expressions/functions, strings containing identifier-like text, LET/LAMBDA local precedence for same-spelling names, reference/function/literal token precedence, supported identifier syntax, and zero/null/`#REF!`/`#NAME?`/`#DIV/0!` propagation. The audit found that LET and LAMBDA locals remain case-sensitive: a local `revenue` does not shadow external `Revenue` when the expression uses `REVENUE`. This is recorded as an evaluator semantic limitation; no FormulaEngine correction was authorized or made. Reserved identifier collisions remain behind existing parser precedence in the general explicit-binding API; pivot declaration validation is applied separately below.

**AH.02 — Dependency namespace.** `packages/core/src/PivotCalculatedFields.ts` now normalizes calculated-field names and dependencies case-insensitively, deduplicates repeated dependencies while retaining the first authored spelling, rejects malformed/reserved names and case-only duplicate declarations, detects differently cased self- and multi-field cycles, and uses deterministic normalized ordering. Existing `CIRCULAR_DEP` and `INVALID_FORMULA` error contracts are retained. The AG dependency characterization and the earlier P1-08T repeated-reference expectations were updated to the approved normalized contract. The focused normalization suite passes 7/7; the combined AG/AH.02 selection passes 13/13. No FormulaEngine source or Workbook API was changed in this track.

**AH.03/AH.04 — Standalone aggregation, result shape, and snapshot compatibility.** `PivotEngine.generate()` now independently computes each configured value spec per pivot cell, including multiple aggregations over one source column and non-A1 source ranges. It keeps the first configured result in `PivotCell.value`; the existing grand-total calculation continues to use that primary value. When the pivot exposes a named-values map, it contains all configured aggregate results and calculated results. Calculated formulas use an engine-owned `FormulaEngine` and the explicit named-binding evaluator; they do not require a Worksheet property shim or a new Worksheet/Workbook API. Names are checked for case-insensitive duplicates, malformed identifiers, A1 references, Boolean literals, and registered function names before binding. Calculated dependencies evaluate in normalized topological order, and dependent formula results are added back to each cell's named context.

`PivotSnapshotTransformer` now carries every named aggregate/calculated result into the row snapshot, retains the legacy primary-value fallback, and includes calculated names in `valueFields`. `PivotRow` and `GetPivotDataResult` admit `Error` so a spreadsheet error remains an error object through snapshot lookup. The integration test exercises `GetPivotData` on a standalone snapshot. Its non-A1 B3:E6 fixture uses reordered Cost/Revenue/Units fields, sum and average specifications over Revenue, and dependent `Profit`/`Margin` formulas; it confirms primary value and total compatibility, all values in the snapshot, and query results. A separate case confirms present empty aggregates remain null while unavailable operands remain errors. Focused red/green evidence: before AH.03, the current-worktree legacy `pivot-calculated-fields.test.ts` run reported 10 failures / 12 passes, including `#REF!` results caused by the first-value-only context. After integration, all tests in that legacy file pass in the final focused selection. No Workbook pivot lifecycle or registry mutation route was added.

**AH.06 — Incremental recompute interaction.** The new public characterization `packages/core/__tests__/pivot-calculated-fields-partial-recompute.p1-08ah.test.ts` seeds a calculated pivot through the public standalone engine, changes Revenue, and compares `ensureFresh()` output to a fresh full-generation oracle. The partial path reports success and updates Revenue/Cost but omits `Profit` and `Margin`; the full-generation oracle produces Profit 26 and Margin 26/35. The focused characterization passes 1/1 by asserting and documenting this divergence. No `PivotGroupStateStore` or `PivotRecomputeEngine` production change was made. Until group-state recomputation and materialization include calculated results, the smallest safe remediation candidate is to force a full build for pivots with `calculatedFields`; that production gate requires separate authorization.

**AH.07 — Workbook pivot API design only.** A future owner-safe lifecycle should keep registry, snapshot store, anchors, invalidation subscriptions, and group state private to Workbook. Create should validate and stage metadata plus the initial detached snapshot before publishing one committed result. Refresh should compute from an owner-safe read view, reject inconsistent source generations, retain the prior snapshot as dirty on failure, and publish the replacement and clean state under one journaled commit. Snapshot reads should return detached immutable values with an explicit stale/read-failure contract. Delete should retire metadata, snapshot, anchor, listeners, and incremental state as one operation, with rollback or compensation before event publication. Events should describe committed changes only; disposal must release all retained state. These are design constraints, not implemented methods or a private integration getter.

**AI.01 — Calculated-pivot full-build gate.** In `packages/core/src/PivotRecomputeEngine.ts:210–220`, `tryPartialRecompute()` now returns to the existing full-builder path when `PivotConfig.calculatedFields` is non-empty or a configured `values` entry is discriminated as `type: 'calculated'`. The check precedes partial preflight, source extraction, and group-state mutation. This is intentionally conservative: every dirty calculated pivot uses full generation, while the existing partial implementation remains available to aggregate-only reversible pivots. **AI.02 — Source-mutation oracle regressions.** Expanded `pivot-calculated-fields-partial-recompute.p1-08ah.test.ts` to compare the published rows with a freshly generated full oracle after an aggregate input edit, a group-dimension move, two aggregate inputs changed in one row, repeated edits to one source cell, and an unrelated-field edit with a dirty notification. Each mutation asserts an additional full-builder call, matching rows, and clean/non-rebuilding completion. The test also checks dependent `Profit` and `Margin` values. Before the guard, a controlled run with only the guard temporarily removed failed at the first oracle comparison: partial rows contained updated aggregates but omitted `Profit` and `Margin`; the exact guarded source was restored in a `finally` block and the sidecar manifest remained identical. With the guard, the characterization passes. Existing aggregate-only cases in `pivot-partial-recompute-safety.p1-08x.test.ts` continue to assert `buildCalls === 1` after successful partial value edits, dimension moves, and repeated edits, with full-oracle row equality.

**AI.03 — AA/AB failure recovery.** Retained the earlier AA/AB builder, incremental publication, full publication, and retry cases. Added a calculated-pivot case to the same safety suite: a builder failure after group-state population leaves the old snapshot published, `dirty=true`, `rebuilding=false`, and group state discarded; a successful retry publishes current calculated values before becoming clean. A subsequent injected snapshot-store failure has the same dirty/state-discard behavior, and retry publishes the current full result. The test observes `DoubleRevenue` changing from 80 to 102 and then 108 as the source changes.

**AI.05 — LET/LAMBDA boundary.** The existing named-binding characterization establishes the local-name behavior: a same-spelling LET/LAMBDA local takes precedence over the external binding (`Revenue` local yields 43), but a case-varied local is looked up case-sensitively and misses when the expression uses `REVENUE`; the case-insensitive external pivot binding then resolves and yields 165. A caller can therefore see a different binding depending on exact local spelling. This is documented as a known ambiguity between the local and pivot namespaces; ordinary LET/LAMBDA evaluation and parsing were not modified.

### P1-08AJ.01–AJ.08 — Pivot integration readiness, formula compatibility, and R1 failure attribution — 2026-10-29

**AJ.01 — Standalone calculated-pivot correctness audit.** Reviewed the non-A1 B3:E6 pivot fixture and calculated-field declarations in `pivot-named-binding-integration.p1-08ah.test.ts`, the normalization cases, and the focused legacy calculated-field suite. The fixture independently checks North sums (Cost 40, Revenue 300, AverageRevenue 150, Units 5), Profit 260, Margin 260/300, South Profit 35 and Margin 35/40, primary `PivotCell.value` 40, and primary grand total 45. Dependency tests reject duplicate names case-insensitively and reserved/malformed names, and identify self/multi-node cycles with differing case. Empty aggregate and unavailable operand cases distinguish null from spreadsheet Error. This audit adds no PivotEngine implementation change.

**AJ.02 — Published result path.** Traced the named results through `PivotEngine.generate()` → `transformToPivotSnapshot()` → `PivotSnapshotStore.set/get()` → `GetPivotData.query()`. Characterization covers zero, null, Error object, missing value-field `#REF!`, no-match `#N/A`, named aggregate/calculated values, primary `PivotCell.value`, and the legacy primary grand total. Existing direct pivot consumers continue to read `PivotCell.value`; snapshots preserve named fields separately. The tested representation distinguishes absent field (`undefined`/`#REF!`) from present null and present Error. No schema loss was found in the standalone path. Workbook snapshot retrieval has a separate stale-state ambiguity described in AJ.05; it was not represented as resolved by this standalone test.

**AJ.03 — Formula binding and local-variable compatibility.** Added a focused comparison to `formula-engine-named-bindings.audit.p1-08ah.test.ts`. Ordinary `evaluate('LET(revenue, 3, REVENUE)')` and `evaluate('LAMBDA(revenue, REVENUE)(3)')` return `#NAME?`, since local lookup is case-sensitive and has no external binding. With `evaluateWithBindings()` and external `Revenue=125`, the same case-varied local forms return 125: local lookup misses and the explicit external binding fallback is case-insensitive. Exact-spelling local `Revenue` still wins and returns 3 (or 43 with `+ Cost`). This is a concrete precedence inconsistency for names differing only by case. Minimal recommendation: define one case-insensitive local-name comparison consistent with the approved pivot namespace, but preserve local-over-external precedence; this requires a separately authorized FormulaEngine compatibility change and ordinary-formula regression review. AJ made no FormulaEngine production change.

**AJ.04 — Recompute recovery.** Extended the calculated-pivot recovery case to cover builder failure after group-state population, snapshot-store publication failure, a source edit between failed attempts, a repeated retry, and a subsequent clean query. Each failure retains the prior published snapshot, `dirty=true`, `rebuilding=false`, and no reusable group state. Retry includes the newest source value, publishes the fresh calculated result before becoming clean, and the clean query performs no additional build. The calculated-pivot fallback remains active throughout. Internal interruption between accumulator operations inside `applyRowMutation()` remains inaccessible through the supported failure seam and is still not characterized as transaction-atomic.

**AJ.05 — Workbook integration decision package (proposed contract; implementation not authorized).** Existing public `createPivot()`, dependency registration, and `deletePivot()` reject at their gated boundaries; `getPivotSnapshot()` returns a detached snapshot after attempting lazy refresh, while its behavior after a failed refresh can expose the retained prior snapshot without a public stale marker. `queryPivotData()` instead returns `#CALC!` when the registry remains dirty. The following operation contract is recommended for a separately authorized implementation:

| Operation | Owner and journal authorization | Staging/publication boundary | Failure and rollback requirement | Ownership restriction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `createPivot(name, worksheetId, config)` (creation plus private registration) | Workbook-only operation; authorize one pivot-definition and dependency/anchor metadata slice. Resolve the source through an owner read view. | Validate and detach config, normalized field names/dependencies, initial full snapshot, anchor, dependency links, and incremental state privately; publish the definition and snapshot together. | On validation/build failure, expose none of the pivot, snapshot, anchor, dependency, or group state. Emit events only after commit. | No raw Worksheet, registry, store, or mutable group-state handle. |
| Internal source invalidation plus `refreshPivot(pivotId)` and lazy refresh through query | Source mutation journal owns invalidation; refresh gets a dedicated pivot refresh slice or a documented read-only recompute capability. | Read one consistent source generation; build calculated fields and named values into detached results; commit snapshot, matching group state, and clean metadata together. | On evaluator, builder, generation-conflict, or store failure, keep the prior snapshot dirty and discard staged incremental state. Query returns the documented stale error; snapshot retrieval must either return an explicit stale envelope or reject rather than silently imply freshness. | Reads use owner views; only Workbook coordinates mutation and publication. |
| `getPivotMetadata(pivotId)` (proposed), `getPivotSnapshot(pivotId)`, `queryPivotData(...)` | Read-only Workbook query contract; no mutation journal entry. | Return detached immutable metadata/results, preserving primary value, named fields, null, zero, and Error under the documented result type. | No partial mutable references; distinguish missing pivot/field, dirty failure, null, and spreadsheet Error. | Do not expose registry/store/recompute internals or Worksheet state. |
| `deletePivot(pivotId)` plus internal disposal | Workbook-only metadata deletion slice, journaled with dependent pivot state. | Remove definition, snapshot, anchor, dependency links, invalidation subscriptions, and incremental state as one committed operation. | If staging fails, retain the complete old pivot; if commit succeeds, no subsystem may retain the pivot. No event before commit; disposal releases listeners and state. | Group state must become workbook/pivot scoped or remain inaccessible behind the owner; no global-store getter. |

This package is a recommendation for contract approval, not an API implementation decision. It preserves the currently enforced owner boundary and leaves the `getPivotSnapshot()` stale-result policy for explicit approval.

### P1-08AO.01–AO.08 — Workbook contract decisions, focused Core coverage, and browser handoff — 2026-10-30

**AO.01–AO.03 — Owner contract package.** Added `docs/engineering/P1-08AO-workbook-contract-decision-package.md`. It distinguishes bootstrap from post-publication sheet lifecycle: the initial `Workbook.create({ sheets })` batch is supported and atomic, first-sheet activation is deterministic, and post-publication add/delete/rename/activation remain deferred behind the current rejection gates. Future lifecycle writes belong to a Workbook journal, stage all indexes/dependent metadata, invalidate/tombstone retained views on commit, emit nothing on rollback, and cannot roll back committed state after observer notification. The pivot proposal covers create, explicit/lazy refresh, invalidation, detached metadata/snapshot/query reads, delete, and disposal. It retains the non-reversible aggregation full-rebuild gate and calls out stale snapshot response shape as requiring API-owner approval. Workbook journal commits are the only owner-event authority; proposed ordering is committed source event, derived pivot-dirty event, then snapshot publication after refresh commit. Observer exceptions are isolated, reported, and cannot block later observers or undo the commit. The existing EventBus and pivot-invalidation Workbook bridge assertions remain contract references; they were not edited to force a green result. No production API or lifecycle behavior changed.

**AR.02 — Merge read identity.** Preserved the original red BT-2 `toBe(anchor)` assertion unchanged. With the 27 generated Core sidecars isolated using AQ's procedure and restored afterward, the suite remains **1 failed, 59 passed / 60 tests**, solely on reference identity. AQ's separate characterization records equal cell values and distinct record identity.

Returning the exact anchor object would satisfy BT-2 but would promise identity across addresses and risk turning a read API into a shared alias; freezing only the outer record does not define nested data safety. A detached value-equivalent record supports mutation isolation and snapshots but explicitly breaks `toBe` compatibility, and still needs nested-data rules. A read-only representation with no identity guarantee can define value/snapshot semantics, forbid direct mutation, and leave consumers to use mutation methods; it must state nested detachment and may formalize behavior inferred by legacy callers. **Recommendation for owner approval:** the third option, with recursively detached/frozen mutable nested data, equivalent values for equivalent reads, and no same-reference promise across calls or merged addresses. This is a proposed contract only; AR changes neither implementation nor failing assertion.

**AR.03 — AlphaVantage throttle timing.** `WindowThrottle` uses `Date.now()` and `setTimeout`, while `AlphaVantageDriver.prefetch()` awaits acquisitions sequentially. Jest fake time therefore exercises the actual scheduling path without a new clock seam. The test records mock HTTP dispatch timestamps, advances by the 10-second window plus the existing 10 ms buffer, confirms six fetches, verifies every 10-second interval has at most three dispatches, checks the fourth dispatch occurs after the first slot expires, and retains quota assertions. Focused result: **1 suite passed, 10 passed, 3 skipped**, in 1.178 seconds on Node v24.22.0. No timeout-policy adjustment is required.

### P1-08BB — Real Renderer Failure and Cleanup Boundary Review — 2026-10-30

**BB.01 — Lane A: renderer construction and disposal sequence.** Inspected the current `CanvasRenderer` constructor and successful-instance `dispose()` path. The constructor validates the sheet/options before allocating a canvas; it obtains the 2D context before appending; it appends the canvas before constructing/observing `ResizeObserver`; then it sizes the canvas, installs six canvas listeners plus window/document listeners, optionally subscribes to the drawing layer, subscribes to the Worksheet, and performs the first redraw. The existing public `drawingLayer.on("changed")` callback is a deterministic later failure seam. There is no constructor catch/finally that calls the successful-instance disposal sequence. `dispose()` can disconnect, unsubscribe, remove listeners, and remove the canvas only when a renderer handle was returned. Source review details and line mapping are in [Lane A](P1-08BB-lane-a-renderer-lifecycle.md).

**BB.02 — Lane B: framework ownership and failure propagation.** Vue, Svelte, and Angular keep the Workbook/view/renderer in local variables until renderer construction succeeds. Their public state/result publication occurs afterward: Vue refs remain null, Svelte does not publish a new store value, and Angular returns no result when construction throws. `Workbook.dispose()` exists, but none of these failure paths retains or returns the local Workbook; `WorkbookSheetView` exposes no `dispose()`. `CanvasRenderer.dispose()` likewise cannot be reached by a caller when its constructor throws. The BA tests used renderer-constructor mocks and therefore establish state publication isolation and retryability only. They do not establish real renderer cleanup or disposal of the pre-failure Workbook. See [Lane B](P1-08BB-lane-b-framework-ownership.md).

**BB.03 — Lane C: actual renderer characterization.** Added `packages/renderer-canvas/__tests__/renderer-failure-cleanup.p1-08bb.test.ts`, which imports and constructs the actual `CanvasRenderer`; no renderer constructor mock or production hook is used. The 2D-context failure occurs before container attachment and leaves the container empty. A controlled throwing `ResizeObserver` constructor occurs after attachment but before event-listener or renderer-subscription setup; the exception propagates and its canvas remains. A subsequent real renderer can initialize and dispose its own observer, listeners, and canvas, but that does not remove the failed attempt's canvas. A second late failure uses the existing public drawing layer: `on("changed")` throws after resize observation and listener installation. Instrumentation observes the canvas, six canvas listeners, window `mouseup`, document `visibilitychange`, and observer registration without matching removal/disconnect; the layer's throwing registration does not return, and `off` is not called. The test harness explicitly cleans captured resources afterward only to isolate the test. Worksheet subscription and first redraw are later and were not reached. Focused result in the main worktree: 1 suite, 3/3 tests passed. The observations distinguish pre-attachment, post-attachment/pre-listener, and post-listener failures; they do not establish a cleanup contract or browser painting. Lane evidence and boundaries are in [Lane C](P1-08BB-lane-c-real-renderer.md).
